cues.en: I'm at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Pasadena, and I'm here to see the first drone that's gonna fly on another planet. It's the Mars helicopter. Come on. What's up? This is our baby. No way. Yeah. That thing right there is the actual machine that is going to take off and land on Mars. It's going with the Mars 2020 mission. That is the Mars helicopter. This will be the first power flight in another planet.
cues.zh: 我现在在帕萨迪纳的喷气推进实验室，来这里是为了看第一架将在另一个星球上飞行的无人机。就是这架火星直升机。来吧。怎么样？这是我们的宝贝。不会吧。是的。那个东西就是真正要在火星上起飞和降落的机器。它将随Mars 2020任务一起前往火星。那就是火星直升机。这将是另一个星球上的首次动力飞行。

cues.en: Now, it's necessary to say first powered flight because in 1985 the Soviet Vega missions deployed two helium balloons on Venus. They transmitted data for over 46 hours while floating at an altitude of 54 kilometers in Venus's dense atmosphere, which at the surface has a pressure of over 90 Earth atmospheres. In contrast, Mars has very little atmosphere, only around 1% of Earth's. Flying this kind of helicopter
cues.zh: 首先必须说明是首次动力飞行，因为1985年苏联的Vega任务在金星上部署了两个氦气球。它们在金星稠密大气中54公里的高度漂浮，传输了超过46小时的数据，而金星表面的气压超过90个地球大气压。相比之下，火星的大气非常稀薄，只有地球的约1%。要让这种直升机飞行

cues.en: I checked. 40,000 feet is the record altitude reached by helicopters on Earth. 85,000 feet is the highest a plane has ever flown. On Mars, the air is even thinner than that.
cues.zh: 我查过了。4万英尺是地球上直升机达到的纪录高度。8.5万英尺是飞机飞过的最高高度。在火星上，空气比那还要稀薄。

cues.en: a cubic meter of air is about a kilogram. The same cubic meter on Mars will be about 15 grams to 18 grams. So you have to push a lot of air down. Yes, you've got to get a lot of air flowing. And so the obvious trick, if you will, is to spin the blades faster. It can spin between 2300 RPM and 2900 RPM.
cues.zh: 一立方米的空气大约有一公斤。火星上同样的立方米大约只有15克到18克。所以你必须把大量空气往下推。是的，你得让大量空气流动起来。所以显而易见的技巧，可以说，就是让桨叶转得更快。它可以在2300 RPM到2900 RPM之间旋转。

cues.en: That is fast. Here I'm trying to work out exactly how fast that is. So I looked it up, and on Earth, helicopters typically spin their rotors at around 500 rpm. So the Mars helicopter will have to spin its blades five times faster. But there are some limits. We really don't want to get the tips of the blades breaking the speed of sound.
cues.zh: 那很快。我在这里想弄清楚那到底有多快。于是我查了一下，在地球上，直升机旋翼的转速通常在500 rpm左右。所以火星直升机必须让桨叶转得快五倍。但有一些限制。我们真的不希望桨叶尖端突破音速。

cues.en: because then you get all kinds of funky aerodynamics and, you know, the transonic flows and things like that. So you don't want to go there. So we, in our designs, keep the tip mark numbers down to below about 0.7. So 70% the speed of sound? Yeah, it was very conservative. One advantage of flying on Mars is that gravity is only 38% of what it is on Earth.
cues.zh: 因为那样会遇到各种奇特的气动问题，比如跨音速流之类的。所以你不想陷入那种情况。所以我们在设计中把桨尖马赫数控制在0.7以下。也就是音速的70%？对，非常保守。在火星上飞行的优势之一是重力只有地球的38%。

cues.en: Even so, making the craft lightweight was essential. Keeping the mass of this vehicle contained during the entire design process has been the major challenge. Every single part had to be considered. The entire vehicle is less than 1.8 kilograms. Whoa. Less than four pounds. That's about the same as this laptop. The blades are foam core with carbon fiber layup. Each of them is about 35 grams. Wow. Yes, it's quite light. Yes.
cues.zh: 即便如此，让飞行器轻量化仍然至关重要。在整个设计过程中控制这个飞行器的质量一直是主要挑战。每一个零件都必须仔细考量。整个飞行器不到1.8公斤。哇。不到四磅。跟这台笔记本电脑差不多重。桨叶是泡沫芯材加碳纤维铺层。每片大约35克。哇。是的，非常轻。是的。

cues.en: 35 grams is the mass of six quarters. Think about that. Two 35 gram blades lifting an 1800 gram helicopter by spinning 40 times per second in just 1% of Earth's atmosphere. How long can it fly for?
cues.zh: 35克相当于六个25美分硬币的重量。想想看。两片35克的桨叶要托起一架1800克的直升机，每秒旋转40次，而周围大气密度只有地球的1%。它能飞多久？

cues.en: It's designed here to fly up to 90 seconds a minute and a half of flight Yes to me that sounds like forever when you're talking about another planet flying autonomously by itself in one 100th Earth's atmosphere I mean come on like that's a long time One of the questions I had was why didn't they use a quadcopter design? Well because on Mars the blades have to be so long that the whole craft would barely fit on the rover Two counter-rotating propellers provide the simplest design
cues.zh: 设计上最多能飞90秒，一分半钟的飞行。对我来说，说到在另一个星球上自主飞行，而且是在地球大气密度百分之一的环境里，这听起来像是永恒。我是说，拜托，这已经很长了。我有个疑问是，他们为什么不用四旋翼设计？因为在火星上桨叶必须做得非常长，整个飞行器几乎都放不下探测车。两副对转螺旋桨提供了最简洁的设计。

cues.en: They also generate lift more efficiently when stacked on top of each other. The bottom rotor sees the sort of the more compactified flow. The top one pulls it. The bottom one sees sort of a more concentrated flow. So the bottom rotor actually can do better than if they were separated apart. But how do you test a helicopter designed for conditions on Mars on Earth? What would happen if you just took your Mars helicopter and you tried to take off on Earth?
cues.zh: 上下叠放时，它们产生升力的效率也更高。底部旋翼看到的是更紧凑的气流。顶部旋翼牵引气流。底部旋翼看到的气流更集中。所以底部旋翼的表现实际上比分开布置时更好。但你怎么在地球上测试一架为火星条件设计的直升机呢？如果你直接把火星直升机拿到地球上来试飞，会发生什么？

cues.en: It would just make a lot of noise. Really? And it probably wouldn't get to full head speed either. Because of how much atmosphere we've got. Exactly. It's like trying to swim in a thick soup. We have a really amazing chamber here on lab called the 25-foot space simulator. And in that chamber, you could simulate any kind of atmosphere you want. You can go to Martian pressures. You can stay at Earth pressures, whatever you want. But that only took care of half of the problem. That was the aerodynamics aspect of it. There's the other part, which is the gravity. We needed a way to fake Mars gravity here on Earth.
cues.zh: 那只会制造很多噪音。真的吗？而且它可能也达不到最高转速。因为我们这里的大气层太厚了。没错。就像在浓汤里游泳一样。我们实验室里有一个非常棒的舱室，叫做25英尺太空模拟器。在那个舱室里，你可以模拟任何类型的大气层。你可以调到火星气压，也可以保持地球气压，随你便。但那只解决了一半的问题。那是空气动力学方面。还有另一部分，就是重力。我们需要一种在地球上模拟火星重力的方法。

cues.en: And the best way that we could figure out to do that was a gravity offload. Gravity offload just means pulling up on the helicopter, so it only has to support about 38% of its weight, just like it will have to do on Mars. And effectively, it was a high-tech fishing reel. So taking a brushed DC motor, a reaction torque sensor, and a pulley, mounting that a couple of stories in the air, and then attaching a fishing string to the top of the helicopter that would tug the necessary force required to offload the differences in gravity.
cues.zh: 我们能想出的最好办法就是重力卸载。重力卸载就是把直升机往上拉，这样它只需要支撑大约38%的重量，就像它在火星上那样。实际上，它就是一个高科技钓鱼轮。拿一个有刷直流电机、一个反作用扭矩传感器和一个滑轮，把它们安装在空中几层楼高的地方，然后在直升机顶部系一根钓鱼线，施加所需的拉力来抵消重力差异。

cues.en: an actual fishing line. Yeah, real fishing line. But isn't that stretchy? Like don't you want something that's perfectly rigid so as soon as you apply the torque it gets applied to the craft? Right, right, and we did a lot of testing with different vendors to find out which fishing line had the best spring constant for us. What does the helicopter sound like? I imagined that in one percent of Earth's atmosphere the helicopter would be pretty quiet. Yeah, you're still at one percent but it's still real loud.
cues.zh: 一根真正的钓鱼线。对，真正的钓鱼线。但那不是很弹吗？你不是想要完全刚性、一施加扭矩就传到飞行器上的东西吗？对，对，我们跟很多供应商做了大量测试，找出哪种钓鱼线对我们来说弹簧常数最合适。直升机听起来怎么样？我想在百分之一地球大气层下，直升机应该挺安静的。是啊，你还是在百分之一大气压下，但它还是真的很吵。

cues.en: Really? Yeah, we have audio recordings of it too. But I would characterize it more like something like that. The gravity offload system was working and the chamber was pumped down. The helicopter thought it was on. It felt like it was on. How do you actually steer this thing around and drive it? So the way helicopters work is they have something called collective and cyclic. So what collectives do is they chain the pitch on the blades uniformly.
cues.zh: 真的？是的，我们还有相关的录音。不过我觉得更像是这种情况。重力卸载系统在运行，舱室也已经抽成了真空。直升机以为自己已经起飞了，感觉也确实像是起飞了。那要怎么操纵这东西，让它飞起来、转向呢？直升机的工作原理是靠两个控制量，叫总距和周期变距。总距会让所有桨叶的桨距统一变化。

cues.en: So throughout the entire revolution, if you move the collective, the blades will change the angle of attack, you'll get more lift. So that's basically what provides you heel control, right? You pitch more, you go up, pitch less, you come down. But then there's something called a cyclic on helicopters, which basically what it does is it modulates the pitch as it goes around. So it can pitch a little bit more here, less here. So it kind of like modulates.
cues.zh: 在整个旋转过程中，调节总距会改变桨叶的迎角，从而产生更多升力。这基本上就是升降控制，对吧？桨距调大就上升，调小就下降。直升机还有一种叫周期变距的控制，它会随着桨叶旋转周期性地调节桨距。比如这里调大一点，那里调小一点，桨距就这样周期性变化。

cues.en: So what that does is it provides an asymmetric torque, right? When you're pitched up there, you get that additional torque. Now you get it, depending upon the stiffness of the system, you actually get it with that gyroscopic lag that can happen afterwards. So once you get an asymmetric torque, the vehicle wants to start pitching or rolling, right? So once it pitches and rolls, you're doing it stably, you are now pointed in a direction and your thrust vector now has a component that's
cues.zh: 这样会产生不对称扭矩，对吧？桨叶在那一侧仰起时，就会产生额外扭矩。具体效果还取决于系统刚度，扭矩还会受到陀螺滞后的影响，过一会儿才显现出来。一旦出现不对称扭矩，飞行器就会开始俯仰或滚转，对吧？当它稳定地俯仰、滚转起来后，机头就指向了某个方向，推力矢量也会在你倾斜的方向上产生一个分量，

cues.en: horizontal in the direction that you pitched, right? So then you start translating in that direction. I've heard that initially someone tried to fly it with a joystick? Yes. An early prototype? If you were sitting right there on Mars and you were trying to joystick it, what is it like? And it's almost unflyable. And the reason for that, it's the aerodynamics of when you want to command a roll to the left because you see yourself starting to move to the right and you start commanding a roll to the left, there's a delay aspect.
cues.zh: 也就是水平方向的分量，对吧？于是它就开始朝那个方向平移。我听说一开始有人试着用摇杆来操纵它？是的。早期原型机？如果你当时坐在火星上，试着用摇杆操纵它，会是什么感觉？几乎根本飞不起来。原因在于它的空气动力学特性：当你看到自己开始向右移动，于是操纵它向左滚转时，控制响应会有延迟。

cues.en: So that delay effect makes it very, very difficult for a human to try and pilot it. You can't fly this from Earth because of the 20-minute kind of time delay, so you have to really send sequences. So essentially, you're going to push a button, and like 20 minutes later, it'll take off and do its thing, and then you'll find out. Right. The way this flies autonomously, it has onboard gyros, onboard accelerometers, and onboard camera.
cues.zh: 这种延迟效应让人很难手动操控。你没法从地球遥控飞行，因为大概有20分钟的延迟，所以必须提前发送指令序列。基本上就是，你按个按钮，大概20分钟后它才起飞执行任务，然后你才能知道结果。对。它自主飞行的方式是，机载陀螺仪、机载加速度计和机载摄像头。

cues.en: an altimeter and an inclinometer. And so using that sensor suite, real-time measurement against the terrain and, of course, the gyros and the accelerometers sensing on board, the real-time estimation of the state of the vehicle is made continuously, again, at hundreds of Hertz. And then that's fed into the closed-loop control algorithm that takes the estimated state and then generates
cues.zh: 高度计和倾角仪。利用这套传感器组合，实时测量地形，当然还有机载陀螺仪和加速度计的感知，持续对飞行器状态进行实时估计，同样是以数百赫兹的频率。然后这些数据被送入闭环控制算法，算法接收估计的状态，进而生成

cues.en: the correction that's needed at the blade level, and then the blades are continuously being controlled. So when you see videotapes of our successful flights, right, and if the vehicle looks dead calm, is coming up and hovering and going laterally coming back, you know, the machines are working very, very fast and very, very hard. It just looks very calm. But yeah, so the blades are being continuously controlled. That is amazing.
cues.zh: 桨叶层面所需的修正量，然后桨叶持续受到控制。所以当你看到我们成功飞行的视频时，飞行器看起来纹丝不动，升空、悬停、横向移动再回来，你知道，机器运转得非常非常快、非常非常卖力。只是看起来特别平静。但没错，桨叶一直在被持续控制着。太神奇了。

cues.en: How will it handle a gentle breeze? A lot of the movies depict... Dust storms? The big dust storms as being very aggressive on Mars. The truth of the matter is, at 1% Earth's atmosphere, there's very little matter actually hitting you. I mean, you're using that to lift yourself. Exactly, exactly. So obviously... So there's enough to lift, right? But we also need to spin at 2200 RPMs to be in the ballpark of lifting ourselves. We built our own wind tunnel that we put inside this 25-foot chamber. How many fans was it, Teddy?
cues.zh: 它怎么应对微风？很多电影里描绘……沙尘暴？大片沙尘暴在火星上显得非常猛烈。事实是，在只有地球1%的大气密度下，实际打到你的物质非常少。我是说，你就是靠这个来升空的。没错，没错。所以显然……所以有足够的升力，对吧？但我们还需要以2200转/分的转速旋转，才能达到升空的量级。我们自己建了一个风洞，放在这个25英尺的舱室里。泰迪，是多少个风扇来着？

cues.en: 960 computer fans, but it does sound like a jet engine taking off. So we built a fan wall array. It's called an open cross-section wind tunnel where you don't need the walls. Just the fact of having an array of fans, we are very confident of being able to go at 11 meters per second, even this vehicle. If I had known that somewhere along the way I'd be building a wind tunnel to do this, I would have probably not taken the job on, right? How long does it take to recharge? We have to recharge the whole day.
cues.zh: 960 个电脑风扇，但听起来确实像喷气发动机起飞。所以我们建了一个风扇墙阵列。它叫开放式截面风洞，不需要墙壁。光靠这个风扇阵列，我们就很有信心能达到 11 米/秒，连这辆车也能。如果我早知道中途要造风洞来做这个，我可能就不会接这份工作了，对吧？充电要多久？我们得充一整天。

cues.en: So the whole day at Mars. Right. But does that mean that you could do one flight a day kind of thing in theory? Yes, by design it can. What is the size of the battery? Between 35 and 40 watt hours total. That's equivalent to just three smartphone batteries. And get this, most of that energy isn't even used for flying. It has to survive temperatures as low as about minus 80 to minus 100 degrees C at night.
cues.zh: 所以在火星上要一整天。对。但这是否意味着理论上每天只能飞一次？是的，按设计可以。电池有多大？总共 35 到 40 瓦时。相当于就三块智能手机电池。而且你听好了，大部分能量甚至不是用来飞的。它得熬过夜间低至约零下 80 到 100 摄氏度的温度。

cues.en: So we keep the batteries warm and we surround the batteries with our electronics board. So the electronics boards also stay warm. We take approximately two thirds of energy just keeping things warm and warming things up to operate. Only one third of the energy is available for flight. Do you have insulation on there to keep it warm? Yes.
cues.zh: 所以我们给电池保温，并用电子板把电池围起来。这样电子板也能保持温暖。我们大约三分之二的能量都用来保温和预热到可工作状态。只有三分之一能量可用于飞行。上面有隔热层来保温吗？有。

cues.en: When you look at the helicopter, right, you have the solar panel on top with the antenna, and then next is the rotor system, and then bottom, what you see, this cube, is what we call the fuselage. You are seeing it now actually uncovered because you're seeing the last day of final, we're recovering, you know, for delivery to be integrated onto the rover. Okay, so, usually you won't be seeing that. So, the center of the cube is the ring of batteries, okay? There is space between the battery,
cues.zh: 你看这架直升机，顶部是带天线的太阳能板，接下来是旋翼系统，然后底部你看到的这个立方体，就是我们说的机身。你现在看到它其实还没装外壳，因为这是最后一天总装，我们正在回收，准备交付并集成到火星车上。所以通常你不会看到这个样子。立方体中心是一圈电池，明白吧？电池与

cues.en: and the circuit boards that you're seeing and then there will be a shell that we put on called a fuselage shell and that will close like co2 the gas around and so the enclosure itself we're using the co2 gas as the insulation material oh wow no aerogel no aerogel we did consider it was in the it was in the game
cues.zh: 你看到的电路板之间留有空间，然后我们会装一个外壳，叫机身外壳，它会把 CO2 气体封闭在周围，所以封闭腔体本身，我们用 CO2 气体作为隔热材料。哇哦。没用气凝胶，没用气凝胶。我们确实考虑过，它曾经是候选方案。

cues.en: It was in consideration in the beginning. And it turns out that just the CO2-S insulator itself was sufficient for us to close our thermal model. And so guess why? We wouldn't want to use aerogel if we have a choice. Wait. There you go. You're welcome to our team. Now, before the helicopter can experience the frigid conditions on Mars, first it has to get there.
cues.zh: 一开始它在考虑范围内。结果发现，光是 CO2-S 隔热层本身就足以让我们完成热模型。猜猜为什么？如果有选择，我们并不想用气凝胶。等等。这就对了。欢迎来我们团队。现在，直升机要体验火星的极寒条件，首先得先到那里。

cues.en: And that's a reminder that not only is this an aircraft, it's also a spacecraft. It has to survive launch. It has to survive launch loads which, you know, easily exceed about ATG. You know, because of the vibration. Vibrational loads are ATG. Yeah. Then it has to survive the seven month trip, complete with radiation. And finally, after pulling nine Gs on entry into the Martian atmosphere, the helicopter needs to be deployed.
cues.zh: 这也提醒我们，它不仅是一架飞机，也是一艘航天器。它必须经受住发射。它必须承受发射载荷，你知道，很容易超过ATG。因为振动。振动载荷就是ATG。是的。然后它还必须经受住七个月的旅程，还要应对辐射。最后，在进入火星大气层时承受九个G的过载后，直升机还需要部署出来。

cues.en: This is going to be on the rover. Before you take off, does the rover pick you up and put you down somewhere? We're going to be stowed underneath the rover, on the belly pan, on our side. And there's going to be several sequences of firings of explosive devices to actually rotate us right side up and then drop us on the surface. For example, the very last thing the rover does is cut us by this bolt and it's holding us, you know, about this side. Then it goes, has to drop us, right? Yeah. So how do you undo a bolt on a spacecraft? Just blow it up.
cues.zh: 这会装在火星车上。起飞前，火星车会把你捡起来放到某个地方吗？我们会被收在火星车下面，底盘上，侧着放。会有一系列爆炸装置的引爆序列，把我们翻转正过来，然后丢到表面上。比如，火星车做的最后一件事就是用这个螺栓切断我们，它把我们固定在这一侧。然后它就得把我们放下，对吧？是的。那么，你怎么拧开航天器上的螺栓？直接炸开它。

cues.en: You blow it up. Basically, the material undergoes a phase transition which suddenly increases the stress in the metal part of the thing and makes the board break. It's called a frangibolt. Then once we're on the surface, the rover drives over us, it gets about 100 meters away, and then we have about a two-hour counter internally where we'll wake up after two hours, wait to hear some RF transmissions.
cues.zh: 直接炸开它。基本上，材料会经历相变，突然增加金属部分的应力，让板子断裂。这叫做爆炸螺栓。然后一旦我们到了表面，火星车会开过来，开到大约100米外，然后我们内部有一个大约两小时的计时器，两小时后我们会唤醒，等待听到一些射频传输。

cues.en: And if we do get that link with the rover, then great. Our base station on the rover would issue the fly now command. First flight would probably be a mutual selfie, you know, you would think. This is, after all, the selfie HR. I like that as the goal of the first flight. Yes, it is. The best time to fly this is at 11 o'clock in the morning, local time on Mars. And the reason for that is we would have come out of the night where we would have spent a lot of battery power trying to, you know, stay warm.
cues.zh: 如果我们真的能和火星车建立连接，那就太好了。火星车上的基站会发出“立即起飞”指令。首飞大概会是互相自拍，你懂的，毕竟这可是自拍器 HR。我觉得把它作为首飞目标挺不错。没错，就是这样。最适合起飞的时间是火星当地时间上午 11 点。原因是那时我们刚熬过漫长的夜晚，期间为了保暖消耗了不少电量。

cues.en: By 11 o'clock, the state of charge would have gotten to the point where we could fly without risking brownout on the battery and then, you know, dropping the whole craft to the ground. Also, 11 o'clock is where the sun would have warmed up things, so we don't quite have to heat up as much. And also, it's not late afternoon where, because of the warmth, the density has begun to drop, okay? And the winds have begun to pick up. Now...
cues.zh: 到了 11 点，电池电量应该已经恢复到足够起飞的程度，不必担心电池电压骤降，导致整架飞行器掉到地上。另外，11 点左右阳光已经把周围照暖了，我们就不用加热那么多。再晚一些到了下午，受温度影响，空气密度会开始下降，对吧？风也会渐渐变大。接下来……

cues.en: What we will investigate is after we get the first couple of flights under a belt, I'm sure we will try to fly in the afternoon and do more exploratory things. But the most conservative thing we can do is to sort of pick a mid-morning flight. So what is the purpose of this mission? The Mars helicopter is first and foremost a technology demonstration to prove that we can fly on another planet.
cues.zh: 我们会在顺利完成前几次飞行后，研究下午飞行的可能性，并尝试做更多探索。不过，最稳妥的做法还是选在上午中段飞行。那么这次任务的目的是什么？火星直升机首先是一项技术验证任务，用来证明我们能在另一颗行星上飞行。

cues.en: The helicopter can take color photos and videos, but its purpose is not to make scientific discoveries. Instead, it is to help engineers figure out how to design and build aircraft for future missions. You can imagine something that's about 30 kilograms carrying, you know, a two kilogram science payload, doing exploration, acting like a scout, like a small vehicle like this, scouting ahead for some future rover. Or it could be a...
cues.zh: 这架直升机可以拍摄彩色照片和视频，但它的目的并不是进行科学发现。相反，它是为了帮助工程师了解如何为未来任务设计和制造飞行器。你可以想象这样一种飞行器：重量约30千克，搭载大约2千克的科学载荷，执行探索任务，充当侦察兵，就像这样一辆小型飞行器，为未来的火星车提前侦察。或者它也可以是一个……

cues.en: gadget that goes and picks up some kind of samples and brings it back to a central lander for more sophisticated analysis. Or it could be a completely standalone craft and maybe more than one that are exploring places where humans and rovers can't get to easily. Polar ice carves, you know, sides of cliffs and so forth. So the real emphasis here is to try to get back all the engineering data so that it can inform that future design.
cues.zh: 小型装置，去采集某种样本，再带回中央着陆器，进行更复杂的分析。它也可以是一种完全独立的飞行器，甚至可以不止一架，用来探索人类和火星车难以轻松抵达的地方，比如极地冰洞、悬崖侧面，等等。所以，这里的重点其实是尽可能获取所有工程数据，为未来的设计提供依据。

cues.en: Flying on other planets will provide a new dimension in space exploration. An aircraft is faster and capable of covering more ground than a rover, and it can provide higher resolution imagery than an orbiting spacecraft. So maybe one day aircraft will be the companions of future rovers or even astronauts exploring other worlds.
cues.zh: 在其他星球上飞行，将为空间探索带来一个全新的维度。飞行器比火星车更快，能够覆盖更大的范围，还能提供比轨道飞行器更高分辨率的图像。所以，也许有一天，飞行器会成为未来火星车的搭档，甚至陪伴宇航员探索其他世界。
